aggregates.claim: A finite ledger over the exact current collected suite, with every execution ID, primary requirement, input/profile fingerprint, current adjudication, declared phase and evidence class bound into the inventory review. Inventory adjudication is distinct from case approval: explicit current needs-oracle or disputed members remain listed, unapproved and ineligible for qualified passes. Unreviewed, stale or falsely labelled reference evidence cannot be silently adopted. Declared-valid runtime effects, other effects, positive admission controls, undefined-result contexts and invalid-input diagnostics have separate populations. Actual observations are joined by exact ID and compiler configuration without adding an execution or attributing a canonical case to this requirement.
aggregates.limitation: Observational infrastructure only: S4.2-001's facet remains pending until the source/requirement census, complete conforming fixture/oracle inventory and separate processor/dependency qualifications are independently established. No finite run proves the universal processor obligation. A filtered invocation retains all unselected members in its denominator. XFAILs remain failures; skips, unsupported modes, missing profiles, unavailable launchers, unexecuted run effects and provisional observations cannot become qualified passes. A compile/link admission is not execution of an interpretation, and a context-only run is not an assertion about an undefined value. Resource failures do not establish permitted size/complexity limits. Compiler headers, companions, launchers and profile observations describe the selected interface, not ABI certification or universal portability. Paragraphs 7-8 are recommendations, not manufactured mandatory documentation requirements.

review.rationale: Renewal of the whole-suite execution inventory after the array element order FIXTURE packet in doc/source_audits/batch_118.json. The member count moves from 2083 to 2089 because this packet adds six executable cases; unlike the sixteen consecutive source packets before it, a fixture packet legitimately changes authored_facets and the case count. authored_facets moves 1788 to 1794, pending facets 5096 to 5090, and fixture review states 1770 to 1776 reference-validated with 274 source-reviewed and 1 needs-oracle unchanged. All 2047 raw reviews, 263 catalogues, 22 links, R402 and the b153c75b baseline remain exact, and tests/expected_failures.txt is unchanged. Six of the eight pending facets of 9.5.3.3 are established: array-elements-form-sequence, position-determined-by-subscript-order-value, and the rank-one, rank-two, rank-three and rank-fifteen order values. The other two, table9-1-is-formula-source and table-layout-ambiguity-recorded, are source and PDF review claims rather than independently executable runtime effects and correctly stay pending. The central question was circularity, since the fixtures use a DATA statement to lay values down in array element order and then read back by subscript while 9.5.3.3 is itself the definition of that order. It was adjudicated not circular: 9.5.3.3 owns the formula and the sequence, the DATA statement in 8.6.7 is a legitimate consumer rather than a restatement, the expected values are independently hand-computed literal constants, and the read-back by subscript is independent of the ordering mechanism. No fixture uses RESHAPE, PACK, TRANSFER, sequence association or any storage-layout assumption. Non-vacuity was proved by mutation rather than inspection: thirteen mutations were applied, including row-major and transposed DATA orderings, same-multiset value swaps that catch an oracle checking only the set of values, a unit-lower-bound mutation that catches an otherwise hidden off-by-one, and perturbed expected literals, and all thirteen produced a failing test. The fixtures use non-unit lower bounds throughout, distinct extents so a transposed formula is caught, interior subscripts rather than corners, and coordinate-coded literals. Every hand oracle was independently recomputed from the source formula with no discrepancies, including the rank-fifteen value of 16, and Table 9.1 was read row by row with its misplaced multiplication sign and stray character confirmed as extraction artefacts. The integrator reproduced both compiler runs before recording any adjudication: six of six pass under the frozen LFortran 0.65.0-411-ga0afaa840b-dirty and six of six under gfortran 16.1.0 with -std=f2023, which reports agreement on six of six cases. Compiler consensus is not an oracle; the hand arithmetic was verified independently and would have overridden both had they disagreed. No LFortran gap was observed. This establishes the subscript order value and the element sequence only, and nothing about storage association, sequence association or physical memory layout. All remaining pending facets, unresolved units, the retained needs-oracle real-BOZ block and every global gate remain open.
